main_findings.claim: Observed Q.output_type INT8 and DQ.precision INT8 are consistent with native Q/DQ class defaults, not evidence of an erroneous custom parser setter.
main_findings.confidence: high for API family, exact binary provenance unverified

main_findings.claim: The inspected 8.5-GA QuantDequantLinearHelper does not call setPrecision or setOutputType; it creates native Q/DQ and sets axis/zero inputs.
main_findings.limit: Not a proof that the installed closed runtime contains no additional internal constraints.

main_findings.claim: Do not interpret generic guidance against additional INT8 type constraints as permission to reset intrinsic Q/DQ semantics.
main_findings.falsifier: An authenticated exact-version API contract showing that these specific intrinsic settings are optional independent numerical hints.

main_findings.claim: Saved DFL NONE success with actual INT8 input/weights and named integer tactic already shows that OBEY is not required for explicit-QDQ adoption in this local graph.
main_findings.limit: Does not guarantee all full-q_all layers, mixed restores, strict instruction proof or accuracy.

main_findings.claim: Internal ONNX annotations should not be changed to FLOAT to suppress quantized types.
main_findings.reason: It is either ineffective metadata for this importer path or an invalid quantized operator/type declaration; changing graph external dtypes changes the IO contract.

exact_version_limit.archived_general_docs_warning: The attempted tensorrt-853 HTML URLs redirect to latest 11.4 docs; those redirected contents are not used as 8.5 authority.

manual_network_QDQ.assessment: Useful only as a small compiler-path diagnostic; not a presumed repair. Native add_quantize/add_dequantize likely expose the same defaults.
manual_network_QDQ.first_falsifiable_check: Separately frozen parse/construction-only pair: same constants/scales/axes/zero points and six-node semantics, compare every precision_is_set/output_type_is_set and tensor contract without resetting any. If manual defaults match parser, the no-extra-parser-setter hypothesis gains direct local support; do not build merely to rediscover identical metadata.
manual_network_QDQ.mathematical_contract: Q=saturate_INT8(roundTiesToEven(x/scale)+0); preserve the signed-symmetric code Clip [-127,+127] after Q, DQ=FLOAT(q)*scale, and identical Conv weights/bias/strides/groups. Per-output-channel scales require the original axis/broadcasting. Do not approximate Q/DQ with float Clip/Scale or omit the -128 exclusion.
pitfalls: Native Q/DQ constructors still impose types; manual network does not automatically remove OBEY conflict.
ONNX INT8 Clip importer already needed explicit native alpha/beta correction; manual placement must preserve integer code-domain Clip and exact graph connectivity.
Native tensor nominal FLOAT metadata can differ from quantized implementation types; do not cast it blindly.

Its result localizes a branch interaction only; if the original FP32 weight is substituted, this changes quantization arithmetic unless code/scale exactness is proven. priority_1_same_corrected_full_qall_NONE.change_only: Builder policy OBEY=false and PREFER=false, preserve INT8=true, FP16=true, TF32=false, explicit-batch IO, workspace/timing and all 88 named Clip native corrections. Do not reset parser requests or assign extra INT8 precision/output requests.

Missing depthwise proof remains missing. Then fixed-image raw finite/repeat/reference checks with unchanged NMS.
falsifiers: Same filterQDQFormats failure with NONE disproves that removing hard OBEY is sufficient for the full graph.

priority_1_same_corrected_full_qall_NONE.preserve: Old OBEY full failure, old full PyTorch/ORT FAILED_UNCHANGED, all weights/scales, raw archives and q_only success.

priority_2_new_consistent_family.assessment: Feasible if explicitly frozen as a new export/compiler family with actual-precision auditing. Do not mix new NONE q_all with old OBEY/PREFER recovery/control engines for causal comparisons.
priority_2_new_consistent_family.common_policy: Use OBEY=false/PREFER=false throughout the new family; quantized membership is encoded by frozen Q/DQ topology. Freeze TF32=false, FP16 allowance, source weights/scales, Clip semantics, IO, preprocessing, calibration, NMS, build budgets and a distinct common-preparation identity.
priority_2_new_consistent_family.nonquantized_FLOAT_handling: For requested nonquantized Conv paths, FP16 flags or FLOAT/HALF hints can be allowed in a declared policy, but NONE does not guarantee FP16 execution. Verify actual FP16 formats for every requested restored source; reject or separately derive explicit FLOAT/HALF casting only if necessary, because such casts change arithmetic and require a new shared-reference contract.
priority_2_new_consistent_family.pure_FP16_control: A graph with no Q/DQ should normally use INT8=false/FP16=true to avoid accidentally entering implicit INT8 quantization. This intended mode difference must be declared. If INT8 is retained for flag identity, no calibrator/dynamic ranges and actual all-FP16 adoption must be independently demonstrated; shared flags alone are not a fair-control proof.
priority_2_new_consistent_family.family_members: Fresh comparable FP16 control, q_all, q_only_G1 and selected restores from the same prepared base; no scale recalibration, changed threshold or post-hoc recovered subset.
priority_2_new_consistent_family.floating_fusion_control: Inspect common nonquantized paths and fusion; count remaining floating/fusion confounds rather than attributing all changes to bit selection.
priority_2_new_consistent_family.stop_condition: Do not launch the full family or a dataset while the first full candidate lacks numerical/adoption evidence; record failure and resolve that concrete layer or reference mismatch.

strict_integer_proof_note.known_gap: Historical full q_all/restore engines have seven depthwise sources without named integer tactic proof.
strict_integer_proof_note.available_tool_fact: Root reports cuobjdump and nvdisasm under /usr/local/cuda/bin; not executed by this analysis.
strict_integer_proof_note.possible_plan: A separately frozen evidence task can map inspector/profile/kernel identity to extracted device code and show relevant integer dot/accumulate instructions plus quantized data flow. Some INT8 kernels use non-Tensor-Core integer instructions; absence of IMMA alone does not prove floating execution. Merely finding any integer instruction or an unrelated cubin is insufficient.

remaining_gate_boundaries: A compiler-policy change does not fix or erase the original full PyTorch/ORT numerical guard.
Freeze an independently justified comparable reference protocol before acceptance; do not choose tolerances after observing native deltas.
Single-image local outputs are not target-level causal recovery, dataset accuracy, performance, memory or power evidence.

sources.version_scope: 8.5.1.0/8.5.10 DRIVE OS documentation; family evidence, not exact Jetson 8.5.2.2 binary identity
sources.supported_summary: Q/DQ boundaries carry explicit quantization semantics; 8.5 requires INT8 builder enablement. Additional INT8 type constraints are discouraged in explicit quantization. OBEY makes unsatisfied implementation constraints fatal; NONE still permits Q/DQ-driven INT8. INT8-input convolution can produce FP32/FP16 output.

sources.version_scope: release/8.5 public header; NvInferVersion.h reports 8.5.3.1, not exact installed 8.5.2.2
sources.supported_summary: DQ supports INT8 input/precision and FLOAT/HALF output, defaulting to INT8 precision at construction. Q supports FLOAT input/precision and INT8 output. Layer output-type constraints and tensor/binding dtype are different APIs. setOutputType alone does not change an output binding representation.

The 8.5-GA helper validates symmetric zero points and scales, creates native addQuantize/addDequantize layers, sets axis/name/zero-point input, and returns their tensors. This helper has no extra setPrecision/setOutputType call. Both tag 8.5-GA and release/8.5-GA inspected; their byte identity differs. Installed parser commit was not authenticated.

Declared graph-output types are assigned to marked output tensors. Restored per-layer precision metadata is a separate path guarded by producer_name TensorRT. No ordinary graph.value_info precision-override loop was found. This does not prove every parser translation unit or binary internals are setter-free.

For the relevant INT8 QuantizeLinear schema, quantized output and zero point have the same integer type, use nearest-even rounding, and saturate to INT8 range. Changing the output annotation to FLOAT does not preserve that operator contract.
DQ input/zero point share integer type; output is the scaled floating representation. Axis and scale broadcasting are semantic requirements, not optional compiler hints.
The native DQ class documents INT8 precision as its only supported precision and its construction default. Thus observed DQ precision requests are consistent with intrinsic native layer defaults.

Q has INT8 output and FLOAT precision by construction; constrained Q output must be INT8. Mandatory native quantized type cannot be replaced with FLOAT to evade OBEY while claiming unchanged semantics.

A later release documents a QAT convolution/pointwise multi-output quantized/unquantized fusion issue with a similar candidateRequirements assertion, and an older workaround disabling JIT_CONVOLUTIONS. This is a different documented context, not identification of this DFL cause or an instruction to change the current runtime.

An author reports the same 4421 assertion on TensorRT 8.5/Orin Nano using trtexec --int8 without an explicit OBEY flag. The assertion is not globally diagnostic of OBEY or a unique layer. No reported resolution is adopted here.
